item.content:encoded: Five people are facing federal drug charges after a sweeping law enforcement investigation that included searches at multiple homes across Pensacola, according to reporting from GJohnsonMobile. Authorities seized nearly two pounds of fentanyl, multiple firearms, and more than $100,000 during the operation. item.title: Panama City Time Capsule From 1976 Unearthed After 50 Years

item.content:encoded:
A time capsule buried by Southern Bell Phone Company workers in 1976 at the company's downtown Panama City building was opened Thursday by members of the Central Panhandle Pioneer Club.

The capsule, which had been sealed for half a century, was excavated as part of a local history preservation effort. The Pioneer Club, which focuses on documenting and celebrating the region's heritage, oversaw the opening of the artifact.

Details about the contents of the capsule and what it reveals about life and work in Panama City during the mid-1970s have not yet been disclosed. The discovery offers a glimpse into the communications industry and daily life in the Bay County community during that era.

item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Public Schools Foundation has distributed more than $100,000 in grants to support teaching and learning across the district for the 2026-2027 school year.

The foundation awarded 19 grants totaling $100,012.75 to individual teachers, schools, and departments, according to the announcement. The grants are designed to enhance classroom instruction and support innovative educational projects that benefit students throughout Escambia County.

The foundation, which works to supplement district resources and support academic excellence, continues to fund initiatives that classroom leaders identify as priorities for their schools and students.

During the celebration, the department recognized outstanding service members. Shaun Cruz…
item.content:encoded:
The Walnut Hill Volunteer Fire Department marked its 57th annual fish fry Saturday, drawing hundreds of community members to the event. The gathering featured grilled and fried catfish, grilled chicken, baked beans, coleslaw, and homemade bread and desserts.

During the celebration, the department recognized outstanding service members. Shaun Cruz was named Firefighter of the Year, while Erick Koehn received the Officer of the Year award.

The fish fry is a longtime staple for the North Escambia volunteer fire service, combining community fundraising with a chance to honor the men and women who serve the area.

The removal comes ahead of the Blue Angels' scheduled homecoming air show in Pensacola, where the team is based at NAS Pensacola. The Navy did not immediately provide additional…
item.content:encoded:
Maj. Scott Laux, the U.S. Navy Blue Angels' No. 6 opposing solo pilot, has been removed from the squadron for failing to meet expected standards, according to the Navy.

The removal comes ahead of the Blue Angels' scheduled homecoming air show in Pensacola, where the team is based at NAS Pensacola. The Navy did not immediately provide additional details about the specific performance or conduct issues that led to Laux's removal.

The Blue Angels, officially known as the Navy Flight Demonstration Squadron, routinely performs at air shows across the country and maintains their home base in Pensacola. The team's upcoming local appearance makes this personnel change particularly notable for the Pensacola community.

item.content:encoded: Delta Air Lines will launch weekend service between Detroit Metropolitan Airport and Pensacola International Airport beginning June 12, 2027, according to aviation news reported on Bluesky. The new seasonal route is part of a broader expansion by the carrier, which is also adding summer weekend flights from Detroit to Bangor, Maine; Bozeman, Montana; and Destin-Fort Walton Beach. The Pensacola route marks another air service addition for the region, offering travelers another major carrier option with direct access to the Detroit market.

item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos announced Thursday that Blue Wahoos Stadium will host a college baseball matchup between the University of Kentucky Wildcats and the University of Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns in 2027.

The game marks another high-profile event for the downtown Pensacola venue, which has hosted various collegiate and professional sporting events since opening. Details about the specific date and time for the Kentucky-Louisiana contest have not yet been announced.

The Blue Wahoos, Pensacola's minor league baseball team, regularly partner with event organizers to bring marquee matchups to the community. The 2027 game will add to the stadium's growing calendar of non-baseball events that draw regional and national attention to the facility.

item.title: Blue Angels close 2026 season with finale at NAS Pensacola Homecoming Air Show
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The opening day of the air show featured the Blue Angels' signature precision flying and aerial maneuvers,…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Navy's Blue Angels wrapped up their 2026 performance schedule Saturday with a high-energy display at the NAS Pensacola Homecoming Air Show, drawing thousands of spectators to watch the elite flight demonstration team perform.

The opening day of the air show featured the Blue Angels' signature precision flying and aerial maneuvers, delivering what organizers called a "bang" to kick off the event at the base just north of Pensacola. The performance marked the team's final scheduled show of the year.

The NAS Pensacola Homecoming Air Show is a signature annual event that brings together military aviation displays, civilian aircraft, and crowds from across Northwest Florida and beyond. The show typically runs over multiple days and draws aviation enthusiasts and families to the base.

item.title: PPD Thanks Pensacola Voters for Approving Penny Sales Tax
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Police Department posted a video on Facebook thanking city residents for voting to approve the local option sales tax, according to WKRG News 5. The penny tax, which passed at the ballot on Tuesday, is expected to fund police operations and other city services. The department's thank-you message comes as the city moves forward with…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Police Department posted a video on Facebook thanking city residents for voting to approve the local option sales tax, according to WKRG News 5. The penny tax, which passed at the ballot on Tuesday, is expected to fund police operations and other city services. The department's thank-you message comes as the city moves forward with implementing the voter-approved measure.

The tax increase will add one cent to every dollar spent on taxable purchases in Pensacola. Police departments across Florida have increasingly turned to such ballot initiatives to secure stable funding for operations and staffing in recent years.

item.title: Multi-agency sweep nabs 6, seizes 2 pounds of fentanyl in Escambia County
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A coordinated law enforcement operation across Escambia County has resulted in six arrests and the seizure of a significant cache of drugs, weapons, and cash, according to North Escambia. The sweep, dubbed "Operation Lucky Charms," targeted drug trafficking activity throughout the county. Authorities recovered nearly two pounds of fentanyl along…
item.content:encoded:
A coordinated law enforcement operation across Escambia County has resulted in six arrests and the seizure of a significant cache of drugs, weapons, and cash, according to North Escambia.

The sweep, dubbed "Operation Lucky Charms," targeted drug trafficking activity throughout the county. Authorities recovered nearly two pounds of fentanyl along with firearms, vehicles, and more than $100,000 in cash during the operation.

Details about which agencies participated in the coordinated effort and the specific charges facing those arrested were not immediately available. The operation underscores ongoing law enforcement efforts to combat the opioid crisis and drug trafficking in the region.

item.content:encoded:
The Florida High School Athletic Association has announced its postseason football brackets for 2026, setting opening-round matchups across the Panhandle and state. State championship games for Classes 1A through 6A are scheduled for December 9–12 at South Dade Kia Field at Pitbull Stadium in Miami.

The brackets determine which teams advance to the playoffs and their path through the tournament. Details on specific Escambia County and Santa Rosa County playoff matchups were not included in the FHSAA's announcement, but local schools will begin playoff competition in the coming weeks as they pursue state titles.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County officials held a groundbreaking Friday for a new fire station that will serve the Myrtle Grove area. The facility, slated for 7209 Lillian Highway, will be Fire Rescue's Station 11 and represents an expansion of emergency services capacity in the county.

Construction of the station marks the latest infrastructure investment by Escambia County Fire Rescue. The new facility is expected to improve response times and coverage for residents in the northern part of the county.

No timeline for completion was announced in the initial groundbreaking announcement.

item.title: SEC Women's Soccer Tournament Coming to North Escambia This Week

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County is gearing up to host the Southeastern Conference Women's Soccer Tournament for the fifth straight year, with matches running Sunday through November 15 at Ashton Brosnaham Athletic Park in North Escambia.

The week-long event will bring together the SEC's top 12 women's soccer programs competing for the conference championship. The tournament draws regional and national attention to the area and represents a significant event for the local sports calendar.

This marks another year Escambia County has been selected as the host venue for one of the SEC's marquee postseason competitions, highlighting the quality facilities and infrastructure available in the North Escambia area.

Deputies say the suspect also attempted to ignite a second trailer during the same incident. The arrest was made following the Thursday…
item.content:encoded:
A Pensacola man has been arrested following an alleged arson incident in Escambia County in which a mobile home was deliberately set on fire with people inside, according to the Escambia County Sheriff's Office.

Deputies say the suspect also attempted to ignite a second trailer during the same incident. The arrest was made following the Thursday evening fire, which posed immediate danger to residents.

Details about potential charges, the suspect's identity, and the circumstances leading to the alleged arson remain under investigation. The Sheriff's Office has not released additional information about injuries or damage at this time.
